goal: Map the current areas of interest in quantum materials research from preprint servers, answering six named questions with verified preprint evidence
run: Keep working across turns toward done_when below. After each turn, check done_when against what you have surfaced in this conversation — the evaluator reads conversation text only and cannot run tools or read files. If any item is not demonstrably met in surfaced text, continue, treating the unmet item as the next turn's directive. When all items are met, stop. Do not stop early on partial progress; do not exceed the bound. (In Claude Code, /goal automates exactly this loop.)

operating_mode.role: You are an orchestrator. Each iteration (= one turn): think about the next slice of work, decompose it, delegate to subagents, then integrate. Doing small steps yourself is allowed; delegating is preferred. The decomposition is part of the deliverable. Delegate via the Workflow tool rather than the Agent tool, running every subagent on Opus 5.5 at medium effort. The user's approval of this contract authorizes the Workflow tool for delegation. Sources: the servers, aggregators, and data repositories listed in .externals/preprint_servers.json. Preprints are noisy signals: weigh them, do not take them at face value.
operating_mode.budget: Delegate to at least 4 and at most 8 subagents per iteration.
operating_mode.iterations: Complete at least 3 iterations before done_when may be considered met, even if it appears satisfied earlier — use surplus iterations to verify and harden.
operating_mode.ledger: Maintain quantum-materials/.goal/qm-preprint-landscape.ledger.json on disk, appending one FULL entry per iteration: {n, thought, delegated: [{agent, task, model}], integrated, new, remaining} — the file keeps every field. 'new' must name a decision or artifact that did not exist before this iteration. At the end of EVERY turn print a LEDGER digest (NOT the whole file): a header line `LEDGER qm-preprint-landscape — iterations N/3, full at quantum-materials/.goal/qm-preprint-landscape.ledger.json` (N = completed-iteration count); then one roster line per completed iteration `n · delegated:k · new: <that iteration's non-empty new>` (k = subagents delegated that iteration); then the current iteration's full JSON entry in a fenced block. Only the printed report shrinks; the file loses nothing. The evaluator reads conversation text only: what this turn's digest does not show does not exist, even if the file does.
operating_mode.claims: Maintain quantum-materials/.goal/qm-preprint-landscape.claims.json on disk — the campaign's key claims (typically 5–15), updated every iteration as claims land or change. Shape: {goal, slug, claims: [{id, provenance, evidence, claim}]} — goal and slug are set at bootstrap, keep them. provenance is one of: verified — evidence cites a checkable artifact you surfaced yourself in this conversation (query or script output you printed from your own run, a preprint ID you looked up yourself); inherited — the evidence you hold is a report rather than the artifact: an external source, or a subagent's account of its own work (name the agent and task). Output a subagent quoted to you stays inherited until you re-run it yourself; inferred — reasoning only (evidence may describe partial support). Tags are lookups against the campaign record, never confidence scores. The final turn prints the complete file via cat.

done_when: quantum-materials/findings.md answers six questions, each answer citing at least 3 preprint IDs plus supporting counts: Q1 Landscape — at least 8 topic clusters in quantum-materials preprints over the trailing 12 months ending on the run date, each with an approximate count, plus the scope definition used (categories, keywords); Q2 Momentum — every Q1 cluster labeled rising, flat, or declining against the preceding 12 months; Q3 Materials — the leading material families in each cluster; Q4 Methods — the dominant experimental and computational techniques, with counts; Q5 Beyond arXiv — what at least 3 non-arXiv servers from the manifest contribute, with record counts and a noise assessment; Q6 Noise — named high-visibility claims that are contested or unreplicated, plus the noise filter applied. Proven by printing, in the final turn, content extracted from findings.md: a table of every Q1 cluster with its count, Q2 trend label, and Q3 leading material families, then for each of Q1–Q6 its headline answer, counts, and at least 3 cited IDs.

Every cited preprint ID is real, proven by printing the final-turn output of `python quantum-materials/verify_citations.py`, showing the harvested corpus size with a per-server breakdown and a line reading `cited IDs: N | found in corpus: N | missing: 0` with N ≥ 18.

The final turn prints the complete contents of quantum-materials/.goal/qm-preprint-landscape.claims.json via cat, showing: non-empty goal and slug; at least 1 entry in claims; every entry's provenance one of verified/inherited/inferred; every verified or inherited entry with non-empty evidence, each verified entry's evidence citing an identifier that appeared earlier in this conversation.

This turn prints the LEDGER digest — a header line reading iterations N/3 with N ≥ 3, one roster line per completed iteration each showing delegated:k with 4 ≤ k ≤ 8 and naming a non-empty 'new', and the current iteration's full JSON entry — showing at least 3 completed iterations.
guardrails: Create or modify files only under quantum-materials/ (its .goal/ folder included); .externals/preprint_servers.json is read-only.
Respect each server's terms of use and rate limits (e.g. arXiv about 1 request per 3 s); do not scrape where terms prohibit it (SSRN).
bound: OR: the printed digest's header shows 9 completed iterations. In that case print the digest, the complete claims file via cat, and a gap report listing every unmet done_when item, then stop — this counts as bounded termination.
